title: Stored physical samples may be accessible to unauthorized personnel
description: When the wet lab transfers a physical sample into freezer storage, insufficient physical access controls, logging, or key/card management can allow staff or visitors without a need-to-know to view labels or otherwise learn that a sample associated with a person exists in storage.
assumptions: Assumes sample containers or storage locations carry identifiers, labels, or handling context that can be associated with an individual or cohort.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storage/access-control activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Sample labeling and freezer placement may enable identity disclosure
description: If the physical sample is stored with direct identifiers or easily linkable coded labels, anyone with access to the freezer, rack maps, or inventory records may be able to identify the data subject behind the sample.
assumptions: Assumes labels, box maps, or accompanying storage metadata include direct identifiers or stable codes linkable elsewhere.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storing/maintaining labeled physical samples; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Presence of a stored sample may allow linkage across studies or contexts
description: A consistent sample identifier, freezer inventory reference, or storage metadata can let internal parties correlate this specimen with other datasets, studies, or prior collections, linking records that were meant to remain separate.
assumptions: Assumes persistent identifiers or shared inventory metadata are used across collections or systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; linkage arises from storage identifiers and associated metadata rather than the biological material alone.

title: Subjects may be unaware that their physical sample is retained in long-term freezer storage
description: If retention and freezer storage practices are not clearly communicated, individuals may not know their physical sample continues to exist and be available for future access or use, undermining transparency and policy compliance.
assumptions: Assumes notice/consent materials may not fully describe storage duration, location, or future handling.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort because this threat concerns transparency around storage rather than the transfer act itself.

title: Freezer inventory and storage metadata may reveal sensitive attributes without direct identifiers
description: Even if names are absent, sample type, collection context, storage segregation, project name, or disease-specific freezer locations can disclose sensitive health or research-participation attributes about the person from whom the sample was taken.
assumptions: Assumes storage organization, labels, or metadata encode condition, study, or cohort information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storage metadata disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Lack of transfer logging may prevent proving who placed a sample into storage
description: If the handoff from wet lab to freezer storage is not recorded with time, actor, and sample identifier, the organization may be unable to demonstrate proper handling or resolve disputes about whether a sample was stored, moved, or accessed appropriately.
assumptions: Assumes chain-of-custody controls may be weak or manual.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transfer/audit-chain activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Re-linkability of de-identified sample ID at the LIMS source
description: The de-identified ID sent from LIMS to the wet lab may still be linkable to an individual when combined with internal mappings, sample context, timestamps, or other laboratory metadata. Even if direct identifiers are removed, the identifier may function as a persistent pseudonym across systems and workflows.
assumptions: LIMS maintains or can access a mapping between the de-identified ID and a directly or indirectly identifiable subject record.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to a pseudonymous identifier assignment/disclosure activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Inference of subject identity or attributes in the wet lab from metadata context
description: Wet lab personnel receiving the de-identified ID may infer the identity of the subject or sensitive attributes by combining the ID with sample type, collection time, study arm, batch information, rare conditions, or local operational knowledge.
assumptions: Wet lab staff have access to contextual information beyond the de-identified ID itself.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to contextual analysis/use of received data; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Over-disclosure of sample metadata to the wet lab
description: The flow is intended to provide only the de-identified ID to be used for the sample, but additional metadata or unnecessarily rich identifier structure could disclose more information than needed for wet-lab processing, increasing exposure of personal or quasi-identifying data.
assumptions: The payload or identifier format may contain embedded meaning or accompanying metadata beyond the minimum necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to data transfer/disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of who accessed or used the de-identified ID in the wet lab
description: If receipt, access, or subsequent use of the de-identified sample ID is not adequately logged, the wet lab may be unable to demonstrate who handled the data and for what purpose, weakening accountability for privacy-preserving use.
assumptions: Audit logging or purpose-binding controls for this flow may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to data receipt/use logging context; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that de-identified IDs are reused operationally in the wet lab
description: Even when identifiers are de-identified, subjects may not understand that their samples continue to be tracked and processed via persistent operational IDs in downstream lab workflows, creating an unawareness risk about ongoing processing.
assumptions: Notice to data subjects does not clearly explain downstream use of coded sample identifiers in laboratory operations.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is especially uncertain here because the threat concerns transparency/notice rather than the transfer mechanics of this specific flow.

title: Use of de-identified ID may exceed the intended purpose or governance constraints
description: The de-identified ID delivered from LIMS may later be used by the wet lab or associated systems for purposes beyond sample handling, such as broader tracking, cross-study correlation, or linkage with other datasets, contrary to stated minimization or governance constraints.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and downstream-use controls are not fully enforced at the point of transfer.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to transfer enabling downstream processing; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Stored raw sequence data may enable re-identification of data subjects
description: Digital raw sequence data stored in the cluster filesystem can contain highly identifying genomic information. Even if direct identifiers are absent, the sequence itself may permit identity inference or linkage back to an individual when combined with other datasets.
assumptions: The sequence data is human-derived or otherwise linked to an identifiable participant, and is stored in a form retaining subject-level granularity.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort from memory for storing/retaining personal data; exact id may differ.

title: Storage of raw sequence data creates linkability across studies or datasets
description: Persisting raw sequence data in a shared cluster filesystem can allow records from the same participant to be linked across projects, runs, or external genomic datasets through stable genetic markers, metadata, filenames, or sample identifiers.
assumptions: The filesystem or surrounding workflows preserve consistent sample identifiers, metadata, or access patterns that can be correlated.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for linking/correlating records; exact id may differ.

title: Presence of stored sequence data may reveal sensitive attributes
description: Raw sequence data can disclose sensitive information such as ancestry, familial relationships, disease predispositions, or other traits. Storing it in the cluster filesystem increases the chance that these attributes are inferable by authorized or unauthorized parties with access.
assumptions: The raw sequence data is sufficiently complete or analyzable to derive sensitive traits or relationships.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for inferring attributes from collected data; exact id may differ.

title: Insufficient protection of data in transfer to storage may disclose raw sequence data
description: When the wet lab sends raw sequence data to the cluster filesystem, inadequate transport security, endpoint hardening, or write-path controls could expose the data to interception or unauthorized access during ingestion or immediately after storage.
assumptions: The transfer path may traverse internal networks or intermediate systems not uniformly protected, or the datastore permissions may be overly broad.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for transmitting/disclosing data during transfer; exact id may differ.

title: Wet lab may be unable to prove what sequence data was sent and under which authority
description: If the sending process does not create reliable audit records, signatures, or provenance metadata, it may later be impossible to demonstrate exactly which raw sequence files were transmitted to storage, when, and under what consent, protocol, or legal basis.
assumptions: The pipeline lacks tamper-evident logging or provenance binding between sample, consent state, and transmitted files.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for logging/provenance/accountability; exact id may differ.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that raw sequence data is retained in cluster storage
description: The transfer to a cluster filesystem for storage may not be transparent to data subjects, especially if retention scope, replication, backup, or secondary research access are not clearly communicated. This can undermine awareness of how long and where genomic data is kept.
assumptions: The storage step, retention periods, or downstream accessibility are not fully disclosed in notices or consent materials.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for transparency/awareness-related activity; exact id may differ.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of raw sequence data from cluster filesystem to compute nodes
description: Digital raw sequence data may contain personal or sensitive genomic information. During transfer from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes, data could be exposed to unauthorized processes, users, or misconfigured services on the nodes, resulting in confidentiality loss.
assumptions: Raw sequence data is potentially identifiable or sensitive and is accessible by software and operators on compute nodes during processing.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for data transfer/access during processing; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Processing of raw sequence data beyond user expectations on compute nodes
description: Once raw sequence data reaches compute nodes, it may be reused for additional analytics, debugging, model training, or secondary research purposes beyond the original objective-specific transformation, reducing data subjects' awareness and control over how their data is used.
assumptions: Compute nodes may run shared or extensible workloads where secondary use is technically possible.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for secondary/repurposed processing in context.

title: Linkability/identifiability of individuals from raw sequence data during computation
description: Raw sequence data is inherently highly identifying. Processing on compute nodes can enable direct or indirect identification of individuals, especially when combined with metadata, job context, sample identifiers, or other datasets available in the compute environment.
assumptions: Compute environment or associated workflows may expose metadata or permit joins with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN categorization between Identifiability and Linkability can overlap for genomic data; chosen as Identifiability best effort. PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Insufficient auditability of access and processing on compute nodes
description: If reads of raw sequence data by compute jobs, users, or service accounts are not reliably logged and attributable, unauthorized or policy-violating processing may occur without adequate evidence for later verification or accountability.
assumptions: Audit logging for filesystem reads, job execution, and per-user attribution may be incomplete or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort for logging/accountability-related activity and may not exactly match the intended sub-activity taxonomy.

title: Excessive data dissemination within the compute environment
description: Transferred raw sequence data may be copied into local scratch space, caches, temporary files, container layers, or forwarded to additional nodes/services as part of distributed computation, increasing the spread of sensitive data beyond the minimum necessary recipients.
assumptions: Cluster jobs may use shared scratch, replication, checkpointing, or parallel file staging across multiple compute resources.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate for internal dissemination/replication during distributed processing.

title: Collection or transfer of more raw sequence data than necessary for the computation
description: The cluster filesystem may provide whole raw datasets to compute nodes even when only a subset, reduced representation, or pre-filtered content is required for the objective-specific transformation, violating data minimization expectations.
assumptions: The workflow can technically operate on narrower subsets or minimized data but currently stages the full raw dataset.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN Non-compliance used as best fit for data minimization/purpose limitation concerns; PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Unnecessary propagation of context-relevant research data into the delivery zone
description: Sending generated research data from the cluster filesystem into the data delivery DMZ may disclose personal or sensitive research-related information to an additional environment and broader set of operators or systems than strictly necessary for the research purpose.
assumptions: The transferred dataset may still contain personal data, indirect identifiers, or sensitive attributes, and the DMZ is a separate trust zone used for external delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for a transfer/disclosure activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Transfer enables linkage with delivery-system metadata
description: Once the research data is placed in the data delivery DMZ, identifiers within the dataset or quasi-identifiers can be linked with delivery logs, request metadata, recipient details, timestamps, or network information, increasing the chance of re-identification or correlation across contexts.
assumptions: The DMZ or surrounding delivery infrastructure records operational metadata about file access or delivery events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for movement of data into a delivery environment; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Sensitive attributes become detectable in the delivery DMZ
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, the delivered research data may contain categories, labels, file names, schema details, or statistical patterns that reveal the presence of sensitive personal characteristics or membership in a sensitive cohort once exposed in the DMZ.
assumptions: The dataset structure, filenames, or contents can be inspected by DMZ administrators, automated services, or downstream recipients.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is an approximate best guess for data transfer leading to detectability in a new environment.

title: Use of data for delivery may exceed the data subjects’ expected consent scope
description: Moving research data into a delivery DMZ for external availability can create a purpose-expansion risk if data subjects consented to research processing but not to broader dissemination, secondary sharing, or storage in a separately administered delivery environment.
assumptions: Consent or legal basis may be limited to research processing and not explicitly cover dissemination through a DMZ.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on the actual legal basis and notices provided; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate.

title: Insufficient transparency about publication to the delivery DMZ
description: Data subjects may be unaware that generated context-relevant research data is staged in a delivery DMZ, making it harder for them to understand who can access it, under what safeguards, and for how long it remains available.
assumptions: System notices or privacy information do not fully describe the delivery-zone staging step.
uncertainty_note: The exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for this staging/disclosure step is uncertain.

title: Unawareness of downstream physical sample transfer
description: The researcher submits a request to the DNA Store so a physical sample can be sent onward to a sequencing lab. If the individual associated with the sample was not adequately informed that a request would trigger this downstream transfer and use of their biospecimen, the processing may occur without sufficient awareness.
assumptions: Assumes the request can result in sample movement/use beyond the originally expected context and that notice/consent constraints may be incomplete or not visible at request time.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort only; likely in the notice/consent/collection-use chain, but exact id may vary.

title: Request reveals sensitive association between researcher and specific biospecimen
description: A physical sample request may contain identifiers, case references, study context, or specimen metadata that allow the DNA Store to infer sensitive information about a data subject or the research focus. This can disclose more personal information than necessary for fulfilling the request.
assumptions: Assumes the request includes direct or indirect identifiers or rich metadata about the requested sample.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity for disclosure during internal sharing/transfer is uncertain.

title: Linkability of sample request to identifiable subject records
description: Combining the incoming request details with DNA Store inventory records can link the requested physical sample to a particular individual or family line, especially if specimen IDs, collection dates, or rare-condition context are included.
assumptions: Assumes the DNA Store maintains keyed or otherwise linkable records between specimen identifiers and data subjects.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; threat clearly concerns linkability during data sharing/request handling.

title: Identifiability from specimen and request metadata
description: Even if direct identifiers are omitted, the combination of specimen metadata in the request and DNA Store records may make the associated individual identifiable to personnel processing the request.
assumptions: Assumes quasi-identifiers or unique specimen context are available in the request or store.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity uncertain.

title: Request may be processed outside consent, authorization, or policy constraints
description: The DNA Store may fulfill a physical sample request for sequencing without verifying that the requested use, recipient, jurisdiction, or study purpose is compatible with the subject's consent, governance rules, or data-use restrictions.
assumptions: Assumes policy and consent constraints exist and are not automatically enforced for each request.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; intended to capture policy/consent compliance checking before disclosure/transfer.

title: Insufficient auditability of who requested which physical sample
description: If the submission and fulfillment of the request are not strongly logged with requester identity, purpose, approvals, and chain-of-custody details, the researcher could later deny making the request or the store could be unable to prove appropriate handling.
assumptions: Assumes audit trails or approval records may be incomplete for physical sample requests.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; exact sub-activity for logging/accountability may differ.

title: Excessive request details retained by DNA Store
description: The DNA Store may retain the physical sample request, including identifiers, purpose statements, and specimen-selection context, longer than necessary. Long retention increases exposure of sensitive associations and reuse risk.
assumptions: Assumes request artifacts are stored in ticketing, email, or laboratory systems beyond operational need.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact retention-related sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Researcher can infer sensitive donor attributes from direct access to the physical sample
description: When the DNA Store releases the physical sample to the NCCoE Researcher, the sample itself may reveal highly sensitive genetic and health-related information about the associated individual, enabling inference of traits, disease predispositions, ancestry, or familial relationships beyond what is necessary for the immediate research purpose.
assumptions: The physical sample is linkable to a person or coded record and the researcher can perform or request analysis beyond the minimum intended scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PA03.09 is used here to represent researcher retrieval/access to a physical sample, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Physical sample disclosure to an unauthorized or over-privileged researcher
description: A physical sample may be handed over to a researcher who is not properly authorized for that specific sample, study, or consent scope. This would disclose personal biological material to a party who should not receive it.
assumptions: Access-control checks, study approvals, or consent restrictions may be incomplete, bypassed, or not verified at handoff time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for retrieval/release of a physical sample is uncertain.

title: Researcher retrieval event can link the sample to a specific data subject or request
description: The act of retrieving the physical sample can create or strengthen a link between the sample, the request, the researcher, and the underlying donor record. Even if identifiers are partially removed, logistics metadata, labels, chain-of-custody records, or request context may allow re-linking to the individual.
assumptions: Sample labels, storage references, request identifiers, or custody records are accessible to the researcher or other parties involved in the handoff.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Retrieval of the physical sample may expose the donor's involvement in a study or repository
description: The fact that a sample is retrieved by a specific NCCoE Researcher can reveal that an individual participates in a study, is associated with a repository entry, or is subject to a particular line of research. This may disclose sensitive participation or status information to observers involved in storage, transport, or handoff.
assumptions: Repository staff, couriers, or other observers can associate the retrieval with a specific donor, cohort, or project context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PANOPTIC id is approximate and tree node selection is best-effort because the disclosure is via contextual observation rather than explicit content.

title: Use of the physical sample may exceed the donor's consent or expected purpose
description: After retrieval, the researcher may process, retain, or analyze the physical sample for purposes broader than those originally consented to, such as secondary research, expanded genetic analysis, or sharing with additional parties. The handoff enables non-compliant downstream use if purpose restrictions are not enforced.
assumptions: Consent and purpose limitations are not technically or procedurally bound to the sample at retrieval time.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; this threat is focused on purpose/consent non-compliance enabled by the retrieval flow.

title: Receiving clerk can infer donor/researcher identity or sensitive attributes from sample labeling
description: A physical sample handed to the receiving clerk may carry direct identifiers, coded identifiers, study labels, site information, or contextual clues on packaging/requisition materials. Even if the clerk is not intended to know the subject identity or sensitive study context, handling the shipment can disclose personal or sensitive information.
assumptions: The sample container, chain-of-custody form, or shipment packaging includes identifiers or metadata visible to the receiving clerk.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for physical handoff/receipt of a sample; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Sample shipment enables linkability between specimen and researcher/project
description: Visible labels, tracking numbers, accession details, or accompanying paperwork can let the receiving clerk link the physical sample to a specific researcher, project, collection event, or participant record. This may enable later correlation with research outputs or other laboratory records.
assumptions: The receiving process exposes shipment metadata or identifiers that can be correlated with internal or external records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for physical sample receipt/linking is uncertain.

title: Repeated sample submissions may make the sender or subject distinguishable
description: Distinctive packaging, uncommon specimen type, project-specific paperwork, or repeated deliveries from the same source can make the sender, study, or underlying subject distinguishable from others, increasing re-identification risk even when explicit identifiers are minimized.
assumptions: The clerk sees enough contextual detail across deliveries to single out this sender, study, or specimen.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether shipments are rare or distinctive; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort.

title: Shipment contents reveal more personal data than necessary for intake
description: The physical sample package or intake documents may include excessive personal details, full identifiers, or unnecessary clinical context beyond what the receiving clerk needs to route the sample. This increases privacy exposure during intake.
assumptions: Data minimization controls are weak and the intake process does not redact unnecessary identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to sample handoff/receipt; exact id uncertain.

title: Lack of robust chain-of-custody could allow disputing what sample was sent
description: If the physical transfer is not logged with strong chain-of-custody controls, the sender may later be unable to prove what sample was transferred, or the recipient may dispute receipt or condition. This can undermine accountability for handling personal or sensitive biospecimens.
assumptions: Receipt, condition, and custody events are not consistently documented or signed.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is somewhat indirect as a privacy threat here; included because custody gaps can affect accountable handling of identifiable biospecimens. PANOPTIC id is best-effort.

title: Sensitive test request form may disclose health/genetic testing context to bystanders
description: When the clinician hands the patient a physical sample request form, the form may visibly reveal that the patient is undergoing genetic or other sensitive testing. Anyone nearby who can see the paper or hear the exchange could learn private information about the patient's health status or care pathway.
assumptions: The request form contains identifying details and test-type or clinic information, and the handoff occurs in a setting where others may observe it.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; likely aligned to a disclosure during transfer/hand-off of personal data, but exact id may differ.

title: Request form can act as an identifier linking the patient to a future sample
description: The paper request form likely contains patient identifiers, accession details, or barcodes that link the patient to the sample and downstream sequencing workflow. Loss, theft, or casual viewing of the form could enable third parties to identify the patient and connect them to the testing process.
assumptions: The form includes direct identifiers or unique codes resolvable by staff or external parties.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; best-effort mapping to an identifying/associating action.

title: Form contents may enable linkage across care contexts
description: If the request form includes patient demographics, clinician details, institution information, and test metadata, it could be used to link the patient across appointments, providers, or laboratory interactions. This can expose more of the patient's medical journey than intended.
assumptions: The same identifiers or codes are reused across clinic and laboratory processes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node and PANOPTIC action are best-effort because linkage depends on the exact identifiers present on the form.

title: Patient may not understand what personal data the form reveals or enables downstream
description: The patient may receive the test request form without clear explanation of what information it contains, who will see it, and how it will be used to obtain, label, and send the sample to the sequencing lab. This reduces the patient's ability to make an informed decision about carrying and presenting the form.
assumptions: The handoff is operational and does not include sufficient privacy notice or explanation.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate and intended to capture insufficient awareness/transparency at the handoff stage.

title: Unnecessary data fields on the paper request form may exceed what is needed for sample collection
description: The clinician may provide a form containing more personal or clinical information than is strictly necessary for the patient to obtain the physical sample. Excessive detail increases exposure risk if the patient misplaces the form or must show it to intermediary staff.
assumptions: The form includes broad clinical history or additional identifiers not needed for the immediate sample collection step.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; exact minimization-related action id may differ.

title: Excessive visibility of patient identity during physical sample pickup
description: When the clinician retrieves the physical sample, labels or accompanying paperwork may reveal direct patient identifiers to people nearby or to staff not involved in care, enabling disclosure beyond the intended recipient.
assumptions: The sample or request includes patient-identifying information and pickup occurs in a shared physical environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; I am not fully confident that PA05.02 is the exact sub-activity for physical handoff/viewing of a requested sample.

title: Linkability of patient identity to sensitive specimen type or test context
description: By collecting the requested physical sample, the clinician can link the patient to a particular specimen and likely clinical purpose, which may reveal sensitive health information beyond what is strictly necessary for the pickup action.
assumptions: The specimen type, container, location, or associated request context implies sensitive clinical information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PANOPTIC sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Misdirected sample pickup discloses another patient's specimen information
description: If identity or request matching is performed incorrectly, the clinician may retrieve the wrong patient's physical sample, disclosing that other patient's identifiers or health-related specimen information.
assumptions: Multiple samples or requests are present and matching relies on labels, location, or verbal confirmation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; tree node and PANOPTIC action are approximate because no reference mapping is provided.

title: Patient may lack awareness or control over downstream handling of the physical sample
description: Once the sample is physically transferred for clinician retrieval, the patient may not know who accessed it, when it was collected from storage, or for which immediate handling steps it is being used, reducing intervenability and transparency.
assumptions: The process does not provide the patient with timely notice, auditability, or options to limit pickup/handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; I am not confident in the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id or the closest LINDDUN Pro node for this physical-world handling scenario.

title: Lack of auditable proof of who retrieved the physical sample
description: If retrieval is not logged or witnessed, it may later be impossible to demonstrate which clinician accessed the sample, creating repudiation and weakening accountability for privacy-relevant handling events.
assumptions: Pickup occurs without strong chain-of-custody controls or access logging.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Visible identity linkage between clinician and donor sample at intake
description: When the clinician hands over a physical sample, labels, requisition forms, or courier packaging may directly identify the patient or clinician and allow the receiving clerk to associate the specimen with a specific individual beyond what is necessary for intake. This creates a risk that the data subject can be identified from the sample and accompanying context.
assumptions: The physical sample or paperwork contains direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers visible to the receiving clerk during receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.01 is used here for collection/receipt of a physical sample, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Unnecessary linkability of sample to other records during laboratory intake
description: The receiving clerk may use patient names, medical record numbers, or case numbers on the incoming specimen to link the sample with other laboratory, hospital, or research records. If this linkage is broader than needed for receipt and accessioning, the sample becomes linkable across contexts and systems.
assumptions: The clerk has access to other identifiers or systems that can be cross-referenced at intake.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for physical specimen intake is uncertain.

title: Lack of transparency to the donor about downstream use triggered by sample transfer
description: By sending the physical sample to the sequencing lab, the process may initiate downstream generation and use of context-relevant research data that the donor does not clearly observe or understand at the moment of transfer. The sample handoff can therefore contribute to insufficient awareness of how the specimen will be processed, shared, or retained.
assumptions: The donor is not directly present or is not given clear notice at the time this transfer occurs.
uncertainty_note: The threat is grounded in the handoff event, but transparency obligations may also sit in adjacent processes; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best effort.

title: Sample sent or received beyond the scope expected by the donor
description: The physical sample may be transferred to the sequencing lab for research-related processing that exceeds the donor's understood or authorized scope, such as broader analysis, secondary use, or retention than originally communicated. This creates a risk of non-compliance with consent, policy, or purpose limitation expectations.
assumptions: The sample is intended for research data generation and there may be mismatch between communicated purpose and actual handling scope.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; this threat depends on the consent and governance context not fully specified in the flow.

title: Physical exposure of sensitive specimen information during transport and handoff
description: Because the transfer is physical, people involved in transport or intake may observe labels, paperwork, or distinctive specimen details that reveal sensitive health or study participation information. This can disclose information to parties who do not need access to the content.
assumptions: The sample packaging or accompanying documentation is not fully privacy-preserving and may be seen by couriers, front-desk staff, or nearby personnel.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC id; exact sub-activity for transport/handoff of a specimen is uncertain.

title: Insufficient proof of what sample and metadata were transferred
description: If the physical handoff is not logged with robust chain-of-custody details, the clinician may later be unable to demonstrate exactly which sample, identifiers, and accompanying metadata were sent, or the recipient may be unable to prove what was received. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant handling decisions.
assumptions: Chain-of-custody and receipt controls are informal or incomplete for this specimen transfer.
uncertainty_note: This is primarily an accountability risk at the transfer boundary; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Over-collection or excessive disclosure of digital sample data in response to request
description: The data store may provide a broader set of digital sample data than is necessary for the stated research purpose or sequencing-lab handoff, exposing unnecessary personal or sensitive information linked to the sample.
assumptions: The request may not be tightly scoped to minimum necessary fields or records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PA03.09 is used here for disclosure/sharing in response to a request, but exact sub-activity may differ.

title: Unawareness of request scope and downstream use
description: The researcher submitting the request may be unaware of what fields will actually be retrieved, how long they will be retained, or that the data will be further sent to a sequencing lab, creating a transparency gap for the data subjects represented by the samples.
assumptions: The workflow may lack clear notices, purpose limitation cues, or request templates that communicate downstream processing.
