uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort for non-minimized disclosure; PANOPTIC sub-activity id also best-effort.

title: Failure to enforce deletion or retrieval expiry in the DMZ
description: If the data remains available in the DMZ longer than intended after recipient retrieval, timeout, or project end, personal data may be retained and remain accessible beyond the authorized delivery window.
assumptions: The DMZ stores the dataset temporarily for pickup and should purge it after a defined event or retention period.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Delivery to recipient without enforceable purpose or usage constraints
description: Once the dataset is made available for retrieval, technical and organizational controls may be insufficient to ensure the trusted recipient uses it only for the agreed research context, creating a policy/control gap around downstream processing.
assumptions: The transfer depends partly on trust, contracts, or external governance rather than complete technical enforcement of use limitations.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance threat depends on applicable contractual, governance, and regulatory constraints; PANOPTIC mapping is best-effort.

title: Insufficient evidence of recipient retrieval and acceptance
description: If retrieval from the DMZ is not strongly logged or acknowledged, the recipient could later dispute having retrieved the dataset, or the sender could be unable to prove what was accessed and when, weakening accountability for personal-data handling.
assumptions: Audit trails, integrity-protected logs, or recipient acknowledgements may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Publishing location enables unauthorized access to context-relevant research data
description: Storing and making the research data available in the NCCoE-managed publishing location may expose personal or sensitive contextual data to parties beyond those intended if access control, authentication, or authorization are too broad or misconfigured.
assumptions: The research data may contain personal data or data linkable to individuals, and multiple researchers or trusted parties can access the publishing location.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for making data available/retrievable; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Published research data may be linkable across datasets or releases
description: Once the context-relevant research data is placed in a shared publishing location, recipients may correlate records with other accessible datasets, prior publications, or metadata, enabling linkage of data subjects or research participants across contexts.
assumptions: The dataset or its metadata contains stable attributes, quasi-identifiers, or contextual details that can be correlated with other information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for publication/disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Individuals may become identifiable from published context-rich research data
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent, making context-relevant research data retrievable by multiple parties can allow identification of individuals through rare combinations of attributes, contextual clues, or accompanying metadata.
assumptions: The research data is not fully anonymized and includes quasi-identifiers or rich contextual information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for publication/disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Publishing exceeds the intended purpose or audience scope
description: Making the data available in a managed publishing location may broaden access or reuse beyond the original purpose for which the research data was collected or shared, enabling downstream use incompatible with data subjects' expectations or permissions.
assumptions: Purpose limitations or audience restrictions exist for at least some of the research data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; tree node selected for policy/purpose deviation may be approximate.

title: Recipient submission or publication action may be insufficiently provable
description: If the transfer from the trusted data recipient to the publishing location is not strongly logged and attributable, the sender may later deny having uploaded or authorized publication of particular research data, complicating accountability and incident response.
assumptions: Audit trails, integrity protection, or non-repudiation controls for publication are limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id and non-repudiation node may differ.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their research data is made available via the publishing location
description: If publication to the NCCoE-managed location is not transparently communicated, data subjects may lack notice about who can retrieve the data, under what conditions, and for what uses, undermining transparency and control.
assumptions: The research data relates to identifiable or potentially identifiable individuals and notice mechanisms are incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for publishing/availability; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Published research data may enable identification of individuals
description: Making context-relevant research data broadly retrievable from an externally managed publishing location can allow direct or indirect identification of data subjects, especially if datasets include unique combinations of attributes, quasi-identifiers, or embedded metadata.
assumptions: The published research data contains person-related information or can be linked to other available datasets.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; PA03.09 is used here to represent making data available/publishing, but exact mapping may vary.

title: Public availability may enable linking of records across datasets
description: Once the research data is published at an externally managed location, recipients or third parties may correlate it with external sources to link records belonging to the same person, revealing additional personal information or relationships.
assumptions: External datasets or prior releases exist that share overlapping attributes or population coverage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for external publication/disclosure may differ.

title: External publication may disclose sensitive attributes beyond intended audience expectations
description: Publishing to an externally managed location can expose sensitive research-related personal data to researchers and interested parties beyond the originally expected audience, causing unauthorized or unexpected disclosure.
assumptions: Access restrictions are absent, weak, or broader than the data subjects reasonably expect.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort for information disclosure through overly broad publication; PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Publication at an externally managed location may be incompatible with the original collection purpose
description: Making the data available for retrieval by a broad set of researchers and interested parties may exceed the purpose for which the data was originally collected or the expectations communicated to data subjects, creating a policy and consent mismatch.
assumptions: Original notices, consent, or legal basis did not explicitly cover broad external publication.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact action id for external dissemination/publication is uncertain.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that their data is retrievable from the publishing location
description: If the publishing workflow is not transparent to data subjects, they may not know their research data has been made externally retrievable, limiting their ability to understand downstream exposure and exercise rights.
assumptions: Data subjects are not directly notified about publication or retrieval conditions.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Publication may make subjects discoverable or infer their participation in the research context
description: Even if explicit identifiers are removed, the mere presence of a record in the published dataset may reveal that an individual participated in a study or belongs to a sensitive cohort, enabling detectability of their involvement.
assumptions: Dataset membership itself is sensitive or can be inferred for known individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to detectability due to dataset presence; PANOPTIC id uncertain.

title: Insufficient publication accountability may hinder proof of what was disclosed
description: If the trusted data recipient cannot later demonstrate exactly which version of the research data was published, when it was released, and under what conditions, disputes about over-disclosure or improper publication may be difficult to resolve.
assumptions: Publication logging, versioning, or provenance controls are incomplete at the sender or the external publishing location.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort; threat is included because publication to an externally managed location can weaken evidentiary control.

title: Unintended disclosure of sensitive enrollment status via outreach message
description: An outreach attempt informing the patient that a new record has been added to their file may reveal the existence of a prior relationship, enrollment history, or other sensitive status if the message is seen by someone other than the intended patient (for example on a shared phone, email account, voicemail, or postal address).
assumptions: The outreach may occur over channels that are accessible to household members, employers, caregivers, or others besides the patient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used here for outbound notification/outreach, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Outreach message can become a linkability/identifiability vector
description: The notification itself can allow the recipient or an observer to identify and link the patient to the 3rd Party Previous Enrollment Entity and to a newly created file entry, especially if the sender identity, subject line, callback number, or message content is specific enough to single the patient out.
assumptions: The message contains sender metadata or content that references the prior enrollment entity or a file/record event.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for outreach/notification activity.

title: Patient may not expect or understand the new-use notification
description: A patient may receive an unexpected outreach from a previous enrollment entity about a newly added record without having meaningful context, creating a risk that processing and notification occur without sufficient transparency, understandable notice, or alignment with the patient's expectations about how their information is used.
assumptions: The patient was not clearly informed previously that record updates would trigger future outreach from this external entity.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id may differ.

title: Lack of proof of notification delivery or patient receipt
description: If the external entity later needs to demonstrate that the patient was informed of the new record, the chosen outreach channel may not provide reliable evidence of dispatch, delivery, or receipt. Conversely, the patient may be unable to prove that no such notification was received or that it was misleading.
assumptions: The outreach channel does not provide strong delivery confirmation, authenticated read receipts, or retained notification logs.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Patient may be unaware of downstream implications of the new record
description: Even if notified that a new record has been added, the patient may not understand what data was added, who can access it, why it was created, or what consequences it may have, resulting in insufficient awareness and inability to exercise privacy choices or challenge inaccuracies.
assumptions: The outreach content is brief and does not include adequate explanation or a clear path to obtain details, corrections, or recourse.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for notification/outreach; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Tool-choice metadata can reveal the bioinformaticist's research focus or sample sensitivity
description: When the bioinformaticist selects specific analysis tools and submits jobs, the resulting job metadata on the Compute Nodes can expose what kind of sequence data is being analyzed, the intended analysis purpose, or whether sensitive conditions are being investigated. Even without direct access to raw sequence data, observers of queued jobs may infer sensitive information from tool names, pipeline selections, parameters, and execution patterns.
assumptions: Assumes job queues, schedulers, logs, or monitoring interfaces expose tool names, parameters, or workflow identifiers to parties beyond the submitting bioinformaticist.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for user/system selection of processing methods; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Queued job definitions may disclose sequence-derived identifiers or sensitive parameters
description: Job submission payloads may include filenames, sample identifiers, patient-coded labels, cohort names, reference sets, or command-line arguments embedded in the queue request. If these are stored or displayed by the Compute Nodes, sensitive personal or study-related data may be disclosed to unauthorized users or administrators.
assumptions: Assumes job definitions contain identifiers or arguments that are retained in scheduler records, process tables, or logs.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is inferred as job/task submission or scheduling in context; exact id may be approximate.

title: Job queue observation can link the bioinformaticist to particular datasets or patients
description: If the Compute Nodes maintain queue entries showing submitter identity together with dataset names, sample IDs, or project labels, an observer may link a specific bioinformaticist to specific individuals, studies, or disease contexts. This creates a linkability risk across jobs, datasets, and identities.
assumptions: Assumes queue systems or audit logs expose both submitter identity and dataset/project references.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to job queuing/submission; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Insufficient proof of job submission or modification may enable repudiation
description: If queued jobs are not strongly bound to the submitting bioinformaticist through reliable audit records, the submitter may later deny having selected a particular toolset, parameters, or analysis job. Conversely, others could falsely attribute a sensitive job to that bioinformaticist.
assumptions: Assumes weak authentication, mutable queue records, or incomplete audit logging for job submission events.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is a best-effort approximation for job submission/queuing actions.

title: Queue timing and workflow patterns may enable identifiability of bioinformaticist activity
description: Distinctive combinations of selected tools, submission timing, runtime expectations, or repeated workflow patterns can make a particular bioinformaticist or project uniquely identifiable, even if explicit identifiers are minimized. This can expose who is working on a sensitive analysis or distinguish a rare cohort or subject-related investigation.
assumptions: Assumes adversaries can observe scheduler metadata, timing, or recurring workflow signatures.
uncertainty_note: Exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id uncertain; used as best-fit for job queuing/dispatch activity.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of final clinical report to an unintended bioinformaticist account
description: When the Clinical Result Generation App serves a final clinical report for retrieval, weak authentication, broken access control, or session mix-up could disclose the report to the wrong user or to a bioinformaticist without a need-to-know. Because the report contains sensitive clinical/genomic findings, confidentiality impact is high.
assumptions: The app exposes report retrieval over an authenticated interface and the report contains personal and potentially special-category health/genetic data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for report retrieval/disclosure during access; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Report access events can reveal linkability between the bioinformaticist and a specific patient's case
description: The act of retrieving a final clinical report can create logs, identifiers, or stable URLs that link the bioinformaticist's identity with a particular patient/report over time. This may enable correlation of cases handled by the same staff member or correlation of staff activity with specific patients.
assumptions: Access logs, request identifiers, or report IDs are retained and can be correlated across events or systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is an approximate best fit for retrieval/access logging context.

title: Inference of sensitive patient status from report metadata or retrieval patterns
description: Even if report contents are protected, filenames, report titles, status flags, timestamps, or the mere fact that a final report is available for a given case can reveal that a patient underwent testing or that clinically significant findings exist. Observers of the retrieval channel or related metadata could infer sensitive health information.
assumptions: Metadata about report availability, naming, or timing is visible to system operators, logs, or unauthorized internal observers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; inference may arise from metadata surrounding retrieval rather than the document body itself.

title: Insufficient non-repudiation and auditability of who accessed the final clinical report
description: If the application does not reliably log which authenticated bioinformaticist retrieved which final clinical report and when, it may be impossible to prove or dispute an access. This weakens accountability for privacy-sensitive report handling and incident investigation.
assumptions: The flow depends on application-level audit logs for accountability and those logs may be incomplete, alterable, or missing key identity context.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; this is grounded in access/retrieval accountability rather than a distinct PANOPTIC logging action.

title: Bioinformaticist may be unaware of downstream use or retention of report-access metadata
description: The application may collect detailed telemetry or audit data about report retrieval without making the scope of monitoring and retention clear to the bioinformaticist. This lack of transparency can create privacy concerns regarding workforce monitoring and secondary use of access data.
assumptions: User activity related to report retrieval is logged or monitored beyond what the bioinformaticist reasonably expects.
uncertainty_note: This threat focuses on transparency to the staff user rather than the patient; PANOPTIC mapping is best effort.

title: Clinical recommendations in EMR may expose sensitive genetic context beyond intended care team
description: Professional recommendations and clinical next steps recorded in the external EMR can disclose sensitive inferences about a patient's genetic findings, family risk, or future care needs to EMR users or connected systems that do not need this level of detail.
assumptions: The external EMR is accessible by a broader set of users/systems than the originating genetic physician alone, and the note content is visible in ordinary workflows.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used here to represent recording/documenting context-relevant research or clinical-research-related data into a system; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: EMR entry can link genetic recommendations to an identifiable patient profile
description: Once the physician logs recommendations in the external EMR, the content is linked to the patient's identity and broader medical record, enabling correlation of genetic-risk-related recommendations with other encounters, diagnoses, family history, and demographics.
assumptions: The EMR stores the recommendation with direct identifiers or persistent patient record keys.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for documenting provider recommendations may vary.

title: Logged recommendations may reveal new sensitive inferences about the patient or relatives
description: Even if the entry omits raw genetic results, the documented recommendations and next steps can allow readers to infer probable hereditary conditions, surveillance needs, reproductive implications, or elevated risk affecting biological relatives.
assumptions: The recommendations are specific enough that clinical meaning or likely genetic context can be inferred by EMR viewers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; confidence is higher on the inference threat than on the exact PANOPTIC code.

title: Patients may be unaware that genetics-related recommendations are entered into an external EMR and reused
description: The patient may not understand that the physician's recommendations and follow-up plan are being stored in an external EMR where they can persist, be accessed by multiple parties, and potentially be reused for treatment, operations, or downstream research-related purposes.
assumptions: Notice about external EMR documentation and downstream visibility/reuse is limited or not salient to the patient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely falls under a document/store activity, but exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Recording genetics-related recommendations in external EMR may exceed patient expectations or stated privacy preferences
description: Storing detailed genetics-related recommendations and next steps in an external EMR may conflict with patient preferences about restricting dissemination of sensitive hereditary information, especially if the detail included is broader than necessary for immediate care coordination.
assumptions: The patient may have expressed or reasonably hold preferences limiting disclosure of sensitive genetic information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping and tree-node selection; applicable where patient expectations or policy constraints on sensitive genetic information may not be honored.

title: Persistent EMR documentation can reduce the patient's ability to limit future spread of genetic-context information
description: After recommendations are entered into the external EMR, the information may be retained, replicated, or propagated through interfaces, making it difficult for the patient to later suppress, segment, or remove sensitive genetics-related context from future disclosures.
assumptions: The external EMR retains entries over time and may synchronize or expose them to other modules or organizations.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for persistent storage in an EMR is uncertain.

title: EMR storage enables disclosure of sensitive genetic care recommendations
description: Professional recommendations and clinical next steps related to genetic care are recorded in the Internal EMR. If access control, role scoping, or segregation for especially sensitive genetic context is insufficient, unauthorized staff or connected systems could access highly sensitive health and hereditary information.
assumptions: The Internal EMR stores the entry persistently and may be accessible to multiple workforce roles and integrated systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; I am using a generic store/record sensitive health information action and may not have the exact canonical id.

title: Genetic recommendation records can link a patient across clinical and research contexts
description: Context-relevant research data entered into the EMR may contain identifiers, timestamps, clinician identity, and specialty-specific genetic details that allow linking the patient record with other clinical, laboratory, or research datasets, increasing re-identification risk.
assumptions: The stored record includes patient identifiers or quasi-identifiers and may be correlated with other institutional datasets.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort approximation for storing/recording data.

title: Genetic clinical notes may reveal highly identifying hereditary traits
description: The recommendations and next steps may implicitly reveal diagnoses, variants, family-history implications, or rare-condition clues. Even without explicit genetic test results, the content can uniquely identify or single out a patient or family.
assumptions: Narrative notes include condition-specific or family-related genetic context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity may differ.

title: Research-context genetic data may be repurposed in the EMR beyond patient expectations
description: Because the flow is described as context-relevant research data being logged in the EMR, the information may later be used for treatment operations, secondary analytics, quality review, or additional research without the patient's understanding of this context shift, creating non-compliance with purpose limitation or consent expectations.
assumptions: The data originated in or is relevant to a research context and purpose boundaries may not be clearly enforced once entered into the EMR.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate; threat depends on governance and consent controls not described in the prompt.

title: Insufficient provenance could prevent proving what genetic recommendation was recorded and by whom
description: If the EMR does not preserve strong attribution, timestamping, and audit integrity for the physician's entry, the organization may be unable to demonstrate what recommendation was logged, who entered it, or whether it was modified later. This creates repudiation risk around sensitive genetic-care documentation.
assumptions: Audit logging, signature, or record versioning may be incomplete or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to data recording/storage; exact PANOPTIC id may differ.

title: Detailed genetic care notes may be detectable even when content access is restricted
description: Metadata such as the presence of a genetics note, the ordering clinician specialty, encounter timing, or note category in the EMR can reveal that a patient is undergoing genetic evaluation or follow-up, allowing sensitive inferences without full note access.
assumptions: Users or systems can observe EMR metadata, note categories, or workflow events even if note content is partially restricted.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate and based on a store/document activity.

title: Remainder sample retained or retrievable beyond contextual retention need
description: After contextual retention requirements have been met, the remainder of a physical sample may still remain in storage or continue to be retrievable, enabling continued association with the individual and unnecessary continued processing of sensitive biological material.
assumptions: The flow implies a retention-limiting event has occurred and the sample should be removed from active storage or otherwise no longer retained for routine access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used here to represent retention/disposal of a physical sample after the retention trigger; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Stored remainder sample can still identify the data subject
description: A retained physical sample is inherently identifying or can often be linked back to a person through labels, metadata, chain-of-custody records, or later testing. If the remainder sample is not promptly removed once retention requirements are met, it creates an unnecessary identifiability risk.
assumptions: The sample or its associated storage records preserve a direct or indirect link to an identifiable individual.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for post-retention sample handling may differ.

title: Residual sample enables linkage with other records or future analyses
description: Keeping a remainder sample in storage after the retention condition has been satisfied can allow it to be linked with other datasets, case records, or future analyses, revealing additional information about the individual beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: The sample has persistent identifiers or can be associated with case, inventory, or laboratory records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen on a best-effort basis for linkability from retained physical samples; PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Insufficient evidence of compliant retrieval/disposal action
description: If the technician retrieves the remainder sample without a reliable audit trail or documented authorization showing retention requirements were actually met, the organization may be unable to prove compliant handling or investigate improper retention/disposal decisions.
assumptions: The process may rely on manual technician action and may not automatically create immutable records of the retrieval event and its justification.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping: this is framed as non-repudiation around the manual retrieval/disposal event; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id and LINDDUN subtree may vary.

title: Use of remainder sample beyond the original retention context
description: Once contextual retention requirements have been met, continuing to hold or make the sample available can facilitate secondary use or access that is incompatible with the original purpose limitation communicated to the data subject.
assumptions: The original lawful basis or notice limited retention and use to a specific context, after which the sample should no longer be available for routine processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping and subtree selection for policy/consent non-compliance related to post-retention sample handling.

title: Residual identifiability from retained physical sample remnants or linked disposal records
description: If the disposal item retains sample remnants, labels, barcodes, chain-of-custody references, or other metadata after disposal processing, an individual may still be identifiable from the disposed physical sample or its associated records.
assumptions: The disposal item or its surrounding process may preserve labels, tracking identifiers, or links back to donor/sample records during or after disposal.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Disposed sample material can be linked back to an individual or case
description: Physical sample remnants placed into the disposal item may still be linkable to a person, case, or collection event through persistent identifiers, distinctive sample characteristics, or nearby disposal documentation.
assumptions: Sample containers or accompanying waste artifacts may contain direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Technician cannot demonstrate compliant and timely disposal
description: If disposal is not properly logged or evidenced, the technician or organization may be unable to prove that the physical sample was disposed of once retention requirements were met, undermining accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: Disposal requires auditable evidence, and absence or weakness of logging creates repudiation risk.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Disposal may occur outside contextual retention constraints or policy
description: The sample could be disposed of too early, too late, or in a manner inconsistent with stated retention requirements, legal obligations, consent conditions, or institutional policy, creating non-compliance with privacy-related handling constraints.
assumptions: Retention and disposal obligations are context-specific and must be enforced at disposal time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Incomplete destruction leaves recoverable biological material
description: If disposal does not fully destroy or irreversibly render the physical sample unusable, biological material may remain recoverable for future analysis, enabling privacy harm despite nominal disposal.
assumptions: The disposal item/process may involve storage before final destruction or use a destruction method that is reversible or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Residual biological material on reused flow cell may disclose prior sample information
description: If a used flow cell is not fully cleaned, residual physical sample material can remain and be accessible during later handling or reuse, enabling unintended disclosure of information about the prior individual/sample to technicians or through downstream sequencing/inspection.
assumptions: The flow cell may be reused, inspected, or processed in a way that allows residual material to be observed or analyzed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for post-use residue removal / sanitization failure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient cleaning by technician can cause privacy-relevant sample leakage
description: The technician's failure to adequately decontaminate the used flow cell can leave sample remnants that later expose sensitive biological or derived genomic information beyond the original sequencing context.
assumptions: Technician cleaning is a privacy-relevant control and residual material can be linked back to a person or sample source.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for secure disposal/cleaning of physical remnants; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Residual sample on flow cell can enable linkability across sequencing runs
description: Material left on a reused flow cell may allow a subsequent run or operator to correlate remnants from a prior sample with a new sample or run context, linking otherwise separate processing events.
assumptions: Residual material survives reuse and can be distinguished sufficiently to associate runs or sample sources.
uncertainty_note: Tree node and PANOPTIC action are best-effort because this is physical residue creating cross-run association rather than a classic digital identifier case.

title: Residual material may enable identification of the original sample source
description: Even small remaining portions of a physical sample on the flow cell may be sufficient for direct or indirect identification of the originating individual or specimen when combined with other lab context.
assumptions: The residual sample is biologically informative and contextual metadata about sample handling is available.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN mapping; exact identifiability node may vary depending on available metadata and assay sensitivity.

title: Inference of sensitive traits from derived research data
description: Context-relevant research data written to the cluster filesystem may encode or preserve highly identifying or sensitive information from raw sequence data, enabling downstream users or analysts to infer health status, ancestry, kinship, or other private attributes beyond the immediate processing purpose.
assumptions: The derived research dataset remains linkable to individuals or small cohorts, or retains sufficient genomic signal for sensitive inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used as an approximate sub-activity for transforming raw sequence data into context-relevant research data; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identifiability retained in stored derived genomic data
description: Even after computation, the resulting research data stored in the filesystem may remain directly or indirectly identifiable because genomic-derived outputs can be unique or quasi-unique, especially when combined with metadata, sample identifiers, or study context.
assumptions: Stored outputs include stable sample IDs, genomic variants, phenotype links, timestamps, or other metadata that can support re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for this transformation/storage step is uncertain.

title: Linkability across datasets through shared identifiers or genomic features
description: Derived research data placed in shared cluster storage may be linkable with other internal or external datasets using sample identifiers, accession numbers, file naming conventions, or persistent genomic features, allowing records about the same person or family to be connected.
assumptions: Other datasets or logs accessible in the environment contain overlapping identifiers or comparable genomic attributes.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is an informed estimate for the derivation-and-store action, not a certain citation.

title: Data minimisation failure in persisted intermediate or derived outputs
description: The compute workflow may write more data than necessary to the cluster filesystem, such as full intermediates, temporary files, excess metadata, or broader genomic regions than required, increasing privacy exposure relative to the research purpose.
assumptions: Pipelines persist temporary files, debug outputs, or rich metadata by default and retention is not tightly scoped.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate; this threat is grounded in the processing/output persistence step rather than a precisely known PANOPTIC catalog entry.

title: Insufficient evidence of accountable transformation from raw to research data
description: If the compute nodes do not generate adequate provenance, audit logs, or reproducible records for how raw sequence data was transformed, it may be difficult to demonstrate that only permitted processing occurred or to contest improper handling of personal data.
assumptions: Pipeline execution logging, parameter capture, and provenance recording are incomplete or mutable.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; the cited sub-activity may not exactly correspond to provenance-relevant transformation operations.

title: Unawareness of secondary use enabled by stored context-relevant outputs
description: Once derived research data is stored in the cluster filesystem, data subjects may be unaware that these outputs can support additional analyses or be reused for future research contexts not obvious from the original raw-data processing step.
assumptions: Derived outputs are retained and discoverable for later reuse beyond the initially understood analytical context.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action id is approximate; threat focuses on reuse implications of the processing-and-storage flow.

title: Unauthorized portal access reveals final clinical report
description: Uploading the final clinical report to a 3rd Party Portal creates a risk that unauthorized users of the portal, or users with overly broad permissions, can access the report and learn sensitive clinical and genetic information about the patient.
assumptions: Assumes the final clinical report contains directly identifying and/or highly sensitive health/genomic information and that access control is managed by the 3rd Party Portal.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for disclosure during upload/storage on a third-party system; exact sub-activity mapping may differ.

title: Portal-side account and metadata can link report to patient and case context
description: Even if the report content is partly minimized, portal metadata such as patient name, case identifiers, upload timestamps, ordering clinician, or organization context may enable linking the uploaded report to a specific individual or episode of care.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores report-associated metadata or filenames alongside the uploaded report.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate; exact PANOPTIC mapping for metadata-based linkability may vary.

title: Portal can infer additional sensitive attributes from final report
description: The final clinical report may allow the 3rd Party Portal operator or other authorized recipients to infer additional sensitive information beyond the immediate purpose of file transfer, such as hereditary risks, familial implications, or other health conditions.
assumptions: Assumes portal operators or downstream recipients can inspect report contents or derived metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; inference-specific PANOPTIC sub-activity may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of upload or receipt on the portal
description: If the portal does not maintain robust, tamper-evident logs, the Bioinformaticist may be unable to prove exactly what report version was uploaded, when it was uploaded, and who accessed or received it, complicating dispute resolution and accountability for handling sensitive patient data.
assumptions: Assumes logging, audit trails, or version controls on the 3rd Party Portal may be incomplete or mutable.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; threat focuses on non-repudiation/accountability around report upload.

title: Data subject may be unaware of third-party portal storage and access
description: Storing the final clinical report on a 3rd Party Portal may reduce transparency to the patient regarding where the report is stored, which third party can access it, and how long it will be retained or shared.
assumptions: Assumes patient-facing notice and transparency about portal use, retention, and third-party access may be limited.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity mapping is best-effort; exact transparency/awareness sub-activity may differ.

title: Upload to third-party portal may exceed consent or permitted purpose
description: Placing the final clinical report on a 3rd Party Portal may be incompatible with the patient's consent, data-sharing expectations, or regulatory purpose limitations if the portal provider processes, stores, or reuses the report beyond the intended clinical delivery purpose.
assumptions: Assumes consent, contractual restrictions, or legal basis may not explicitly cover third-party portal processing or secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity for consent/purpose non-compliance may differ.

title: Mis-upload by Bioinformaticist discloses report to wrong portal location or recipient
description: During upload, the Bioinformaticist could select the wrong patient record, case workspace, or recipient context in the 3rd Party Portal, causing the final clinical report to be disclosed to an unintended party.
assumptions: Assumes the portal interface permits manual selection of patient/case destinations and that human error is possible.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is an approximate best fit for the act of uploading/sharing via a portal.

title: Unauthorized portal access exposes final clinical report to the wrong counselor or third party
description: If access control on the 3rd Party Portal is weak or misconfigured, a person other than the intended Genetic Counselor could download the final clinical report, disclosing sensitive genetic and clinical information.
assumptions: The portal stores reports for multiple patients and/or multiple counselor accounts, and access is mediated by authentication and authorization controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for portal-mediated disclosure during report access/download; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Portal records can identify which counselor accessed which patient's final report
description: Download and access logs on the 3rd Party Portal may link the Genetic Counselor to a specific patient's final clinical report, enabling inference about the counselor-patient relationship and the patient's involvement in genetic testing.
assumptions: The portal maintains detailed per-user audit logs and those logs are accessible to portal operators, administrators, or other parties.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for access/download logging context.

title: Genetic Counselor may be unaware of portal-side collection and reuse of download metadata
description: When downloading the final clinical report, the Genetic Counselor may not be adequately informed that the portal collects metadata such as timestamps, IP address, device/browser details, and report identifiers, and may retain or reuse that metadata beyond what the counselor expects.
assumptions: The portal captures telemetry or audit metadata during downloads and transparency notice or consent/choice mechanisms are limited.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; uncertain exact sub-activity id for metadata collection during report download.

title: Excessive download telemetry or embedded identifiers create detectability of report retrieval events
description: Network, portal, or report-download telemetry may make it observable that a final clinical report was retrieved at a particular time, allowing operators or observers with access to logs to detect the occurrence of a sensitive clinical event even if they do not view the report contents.
assumptions: Download events generate observable metadata such as URLs, object identifiers, timestamps, or content-disposition details in logs.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort because detectability branches vary by threat-tree version; PANOPTIC id also approximate.

title: Portal-side identifiers enable linking repeated report downloads across patients or cases
description: Persistent account identifiers, session identifiers, or download tokens on the portal could allow portal operators or integrated third parties to link multiple report retrievals by the same Genetic Counselor, building a profile of the counselor's caseload or patient interactions.
assumptions: The portal uses stable user/account identifiers or correlatable telemetry across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping and tree node selection for linking through persistent portal identifiers.

title: Insufficient proof around report download could enable repudiation disputes
description: If download logging is incomplete or weakly bound to the counselor's authenticated session, the Genetic Counselor could later dispute having downloaded the final report, or the organization could be unable to prove who accessed it, undermining accountability for sensitive report handling.
assumptions: Audit integrity, session binding, or non-repudiation controls may be weak.
uncertainty_note: Included because accountability of sensitive report access can have privacy implications; PANOPTIC mapping approximate.

title: Over-disclosure of context-relevant research data to clinician
description: The genetic counselor makes context-relevant clinical/research data available for retrieval with additional input and analysis. If the dataset includes more genetic or related contextual information than the clinician needs for the stated purpose, the clinician may learn sensitive details beyond necessity.
assumptions: Assumes access controls or data filtering may not strictly enforce minimum necessary disclosure for this retrieval flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used to represent making data available for retrieval/analysis, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Secondary use of retrieved genetic/research context by clinician
description: After retrieving the context-relevant research data and combining it with additional input and analysis, the clinician could use the data for purposes not originally expected by the patient, such as broader profiling, research, or care decisions outside the initial context.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation is not fully enforced or downstream use is not transparently governed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for downstream analysis and reuse may differ from PA03.09.

title: Linkability through combination with additional clinical input
description: Because the clinician retrieves the data specifically to add further input and analysis, the flow enables linking the genetic/research context with other clinical records or observations, potentially creating a richer identifiable profile across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the clinician has access to other datasets or patient records that can be correlated with this flow.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; threat is grounded in retrieval plus enrichment/analysis across datasets.

title: Identifiability from context-rich genetic information
description: Even if the shared data is described as context-relevant research data, genetic and related clinical context can be inherently identifying or become identifying once the clinician adds local context and analysis.
assumptions: Assumes the data contains genomic or highly specific phenotypic/contextual attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact sub-activity id for retrieval and enrichment may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent alignment for clinician retrieval and analysis
description: The patient may not expect that context-relevant research data supplied by the genetic counselor will be retrieved by the clinician and further analyzed with added input. This can create a non-compliance risk if consent, notice, or policy does not clearly cover this transfer and downstream processing.
assumptions: Assumes consent scope, notice, or legal basis for this particular retrieval-and-analysis step may be ambiguous or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes from additional analysis
description: The clinician's additional input and analysis may derive new sensitive conclusions from the retrieved data, such as disease risks, familial implications, or reproductive information, disclosing information that was not explicit in the original shared dataset.
assumptions: Assumes analytic enrichment can produce novel sensitive inferences from the transferred research/contextual data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; using PA03.09 as a best-effort anchor for retrieval plus analysis.

title: Residual genomic data remains on decommissioned wet-lab devices
description: If storage media, firmware caches, embedded controllers, or removable components on privacy-relevant wet-lab devices are not securely sanitized before resale or disposal, genomic and associated personal data may remain recoverable by subsequent owners or service personnel, causing unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: The devices may contain local storage, logs, temporary files, calibration/export data, or cached genomic processing data that persist beyond operational use.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for insecure decommissioning/media sanitization; exact mapping may vary.

title: Lack of verifiable proof of secure decommissioning
description: If the Device Decommissioning Specialist cannot produce reliable evidence that each device was wiped, destroyed, or sanitized according to policy, the organization may be unable to prove compliant handling of personal/genomic data and may later be unable to refute claims that decommissioning was performed improperly.
assumptions: The process relies on human execution and may lack tamper-evident certificates, chain-of-custody records, or audit logs for each device.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for decommissioning-related accountability gaps; exact mapping may vary.

title: Incomplete decommissioning process leaves hidden storage or backups unsanitized
description: The decommissioning specialist may be unaware of all locations where privacy-relevant data reside on the device, such as hidden partitions, instrument logs, removable media, maintenance backups, or cloud-synced components. This can leave personal/genomic data exposed after resale.
assumptions: Wet-lab devices can contain non-obvious storage locations or vendor-specific service areas not covered by standard wipe procedures.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; uncertainty is mainly in the exact sub-activity id, not in the threat applicability.

title: Decommissioning practice fails to meet data-retention and disposal obligations
description: If devices are resold without privacy-preserving sanitization or documented destruction, the organization may violate contractual, regulatory, or policy requirements governing disposal of genomic and personal data.
assumptions: Applicable obligations require secure disposal/sanitization and possibly documentation before transfer or resale.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for non-compliant decommissioning/disposal.

title: Residual genomic/patient data present on acquired refurbished wet-lab device
description: A refurbished or previously used wet-lab device may retain stored genomic, patient, run-history, configuration, or audit data from prior use. When the organization acquires and brings the device into its environment, that residual data can be disclosed to unauthorized parties, creating a privacy breach.
assumptions: The device contains internal storage, firmware logs, caches, or attached media that may persist data across ownership changes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: this is grounded in procurement/acquisition of a device with residual data; PA05.02 is an approximate sub-activity identifier.

title: Procurement from non-trusted or non-compliant refurbishment source increases disclosure risk
description: If the Device Acquisition Specialist procures devices from manufacturers or refurbishers that do not follow privacy-preserving sanitization and reset practices, sensitive data from previous operators may be unintentionally disclosed to the acquiring organization or downstream users.
assumptions: The acquisition process includes selecting vendors/refurbishers and accepting devices without independently verifying sanitization evidence.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely falls under acquisition/provisioning-related activity, but the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Unclear provenance and sanitization history of acquired device prevents determining prior data handling
description: If the acquired device lacks trustworthy records of prior ownership, servicing, and sanitization, data subjects and operators may be unable to determine whether personal data remains on the device or was previously exposed. This impairs accountability and incident investigation around inherited data.
assumptions: The organization relies on vendor/refurbisher attestations or incomplete asset-history documentation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because this is an identifiability/detectability-adjacent issue in some interpretations; PANOPTIC action id is approximate.

title: Acquisition of devices without privacy-best-practice refurbishment may violate sanitization obligations
description: Purchasing wet-lab devices that were not newly manufactured or properly refurbished/sanitized may put the organization out of compliance with legal, contractual, or policy obligations requiring secure erasure and protection of personal data during asset transfer.
assumptions: Applicable policies, contracts, or regulations require secure media sanitization and due diligence on acquired devices.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id may differ.
